userStories.title: Typed Spec schema + validators in src/issues/spec.ts
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a typed Spec interface and pure validators so the spec field stops being unknown and downstream writers can validate structured specs and WSJF before committing.
acceptanceCriteria: src/issues/spec.ts exports a Spec interface { acceptanceCriteria: string[]; scope: string; gotchas: string[]; domainTerms: string[] }. [oracle: grep -q 'interface Spec' src/issues/spec.ts]
IssueEntry.spec is typed as Spec (optional) instead of unknown in src/issues/types.ts. [oracle: grep -q 'spec?: Spec' src/issues/types.ts]
validateSpec(x) returns { ok: boolean; errors: string[] }, rejecting missing/empty acceptanceCriteria and missing scope. [oracle: bun test]
validateWsjf(x) returns { ok, errors } and rejects a WsjfScore missing any of the four components value/timeCriticality/riskReduction/jobSize. [oracle: bun test]
Unit tests cover valid and each invalid shape for both validators. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
biome lint passes (bun run lint). [oracle: bun run lint]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: New module src/issues/spec.ts; test under test/issues/spec.test.ts. Reuse WsjfScore from src/issues/types.ts (do not redefine: import it). Changing IssueEntry.spec from unknown to Spec? may surface type errors at any existing reader of .spec: run `bun run typecheck` and guard with noUncheckedIndexedAccess in mind (array access is T|undefined). Validators are PURE (no I/O), mirroring src/issues/graph.ts checkReferentialIntegrity shape { ok, errors }. Domain term: a 'spec' is the structured deep-spec written by the grill (AC + scope + gotchas + domainTerms), distinct from the free-text description captured at stage:idea.

userStories.title: Deterministic spec writer specifyIssueOnMain (promote idea->specified on main)
userStories.description: As the grill flow, I need a deterministic writer that sets spec + blockedBy + wsjf and flips stage idea->specified for an existing issue id, committing on main without touching the work branch, so the grill's structured output lands in the backlog from any branch.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/issue-specify.ts exports specifyIssueOnMain that reads the backlog via `git show main:scripts/cam/issues.local.json` and never runs `git checkout` (mirrors issue-file.ts commit-tree-on-main). [oracle: grep -q 'show' src/commands/issue-specify.ts && ! grep -q 'checkout' src/commands/issue-specify.ts]
It validates the spec (validateSpec) and wsjf (validateWsjf) and returns an error outcome without committing when invalid. [oracle: bun test]
It guards that the target id exists and is currently stage:'idea' AND status:'open', returning a typed error otherwise (no mutation). [oracle: bun test]
It runs checkReferentialIntegrity (src/issues/graph.ts) on the post-write backlog and refuses to commit when integrity fails. [oracle: bun test]
On success it writes spec + blockedBy + wsjf and sets stage:'specified', committed to main via commit-tree plumbing. [oracle: bun test]
Real-git regression tests exercise the full commit-tree path in a temp repo (mirror issue-file's test style). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
biome lint passes (bun run lint). [oracle: bun run lint]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: New module src/commands/issue-specify.ts; tests under test/commands/issue-specify.test.ts. CANONICAL pattern to mirror: src/commands/issue-file.ts (createLocalIssueOnMain) -- DI'd synchronous SpawnFn + ClockFn, on-main path (write/add/commit) vs off-main commit-tree plumbing (temp GIT_INDEX_FILE, read-tree, hash-object -w --stdin, update-index --cacheinfo, write-tree, commit-tree -p main, update-ref refs/heads/main). Reference src/commands/ship-finalize.ts for the stage-write approach (it sets stage:'shipped'). Import validateSpec/validateWsjf from US-002, isBlocked/checkReferentialIntegrity from src/issues/graph.ts. Commit msg style: `chore(cam): specify <id>`. NEVER touch the work branch (the whole point: idea filed/specified on main while a feature branch is open). Lesson (issues-local-next-id-multiwriter): a live `cam run` is a concurrent writer of issues.local.json -- read from main, write via plumbing, do not assume working-tree is canonical.

userStories.description: As an operator diagnosing the loop, I need a structured spec-written / stage-promoted event emitted at the real writer call-site so a grill promotion is replayable, not just observable in a test fake.
acceptanceCriteria: The spec writer emits a structured event (e.g. kind 'spec-written' or 'stage-promoted') carrying { id, fromStage, toStage } via the injected event sink. [oracle: bun test]

The default file event sink is wired at the REAL call-site in src/commands/issue-specify.ts via makeFileEventLogger (the canonical production sink factory in src/supervisor/events.ts), not only injected in a test. [oracle: grep -q 'makeFileEventLogger' src/commands/issue-specify.ts]
A production-wiring test fails if the sink is left unwired (asserts the default path emits, not just the injected fake). [oracle: bun test]

biome lint passes (bun run lint). [oracle: bun run lint]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Event types live in src/supervisor/events.ts (WorkerEventKind union + appendFileSync default sink to .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl). Add the new kind to the union and emit from the writer. CRITICAL anti-pattern (CAM-53/89, sidecar-stale-worker-pane / fake-spawn-masks-dead-production): a test that only exercises the INJECTED sink proves nothing about production; the wiring test must drive the DEFAULT (real) sink path so an unwired default fails the gate. The event log is supervisor-owned in the loop, but this writer is operator-invoked (grill), so the writer owns its own emit. Keep the emit a side effect of a successful commit only (do not emit on validation/guard failure).

userStories.title: Dogfood: grill one real idea end-to-end to stage:specified
userStories.description: As the operator, I need to grill one real idea through /cam-spec to stage:specified so the no-arg cam plan gate has a selectable issue, proving the flow end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one issue in issues.local.json on main reaches stage:'specified' with status:'open'. [oracle: git show main:scripts/cam/issues.local.json | grep -q '"specified"']
selectPlannableIssue would return that issue (stage:'specified', status:'open', not blocked), making the no-arg cam plan gate non-empty. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
The promoted issue carries a valid spec (AC + scope + gotchas + domainTerms) and wsjf with all four components. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
userStories.notes: OPERATOR CEREMONY: the grill is an interactive in-session interview (16-50 questions, one at a time, codebase-first, recommends answers); it cannot be driven autonomously. The implementer exits BLOCKED_OPERATOR_REQUIRED; the operator hand-runs /cam-spec <id> against a real idea, lands stage:'specified' on main, then flips passes:true and re-runs cam next. This unblocks Epicos C and D and gives `cam plan` (no-arg) a selectable issue (src/issues/select.ts selectPlannableIssue). No mandatory typecheck/test criteria: this story writes no source, only exercises the shipped flow and lands a data change on main.
